findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type and uses raw UserUID, causing cross-identity collisions
findings.body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` is constructed using `checkReq.UserUID` directly without incorporating `checkReq.IdentityType` or resolving `checkReq.UserUID` to the canonical `userIdentifiers.UID`. This causes two problems:
1. Different identity types can share the same `UserUID` (e.g., `anonymous:0`, `render:0`, `user:0`, or `service-account:0` all have `UserUID == "0"`). If `anonymous:0` is denied access to a resource (such as `dashboards:read`), that denial is cached under `0` and will subsequently block `render:0` or `user:0` from accessing the same resource until the cache expires.
2. `GetUserIdentifiers` accepts either a numeric internal ID or a string UID, and `permCache` keys on the resolved `userIdentifiers.UID`. Because `permDenialCache` keys on the raw `checkReq.UserUID`, denial cache entries will not be shared between requests using the numeric ID and requests using the string UID.

findings.title: Outdated folder tree cache prevents newly created subfolders or items in new subfolders from being accessed
findings.body: When a permission check against `cachedPerms` returns `false`, `Check` re-queries user permissions from the database via `getIdentityPermissions` and re-runs `checkPermission`. However, `checkPermission` calls `checkInheritedPermissions` -> `buildFolderTree`, which still reads from `s.folderCache` without invalidating or bypassing it. If a user creates a subfolder inside a folder they have permissions on (where access is granted via inheritance from the parent folder rather than a direct permission on the new subfolder) or creates a dashboard inside a newly created subfolder, `buildFolderTree` will return the stale cached folder tree that does not contain the new subfolder, causing `Check` to return `Allowed: false` and cache the denial in `permDenialCache` for `shortCacheTTL`.

findings.title: Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets permission map value to false instead of true
findings.body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` ('Should deny on explicit cache deny entry'), the comment states `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`, but line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. Even if `permDenialCache` were completely ignored, `permCache` would still evaluate to `false` (and fall through to the empty `fakeStore`, which also returns `false`). To actually verify that `permDenialCache` takes precedence over `permCache`, the map value in `permCache` must be `true`.
